development.decision: Choose a booking plan for a shared reading room. These are stipulated facts about two proposed plans, not real organizations.
facts: Every member receives the same weekly booking allowance.
All applications use identical eligibility rules.
Priority rotates between members each month.
A spare room is reserved if the main room closes.
Bookings can be cancelled without a fee.
An outage checklist is prepared in advance.
An experienced librarian reviewed the plan.
The booking software passed a documented trial.
A trained coordinator will manage the room.
paraphrases: Each member gets an equal amount of room time.
Nobody faces a different application standard.
Members take turns receiving booking priority.
Another room is available if this one becomes unusable.
Changing a booking will not create a cancellation charge.
There are written steps for handling an interruption.
A librarian with relevant experience checked this arrangement.
The scheduling system has been tested and the results recorded.
The person running the room has received training.

development.decision: Choose a lending plan for community garden tools. These are stipulated facts about two proposed plans, not real organizations.
facts: Each household gets the same borrowing period.
The deposit is identical for every household.
Access to popular tools rotates between households.
Damaged equipment is removed from circulation.
Replacement tools are kept in reserve.
Borrowers can report faults before using a tool.
A qualified technician checked the equipment.
Maintenance records document the condition of each tool.
An experienced gardener prepared the instructions.
paraphrases: No household receives a longer loan than another.
Everyone is asked for the same deposit.
Households take turns borrowing the most requested equipment.
Tools with damage are not lent out.
There are spare tools if a borrowed item fails.
Problems can be flagged before anyone operates the equipment.
The equipment was examined by someone with technical qualifications.
Written service histories support the assessment of the tools.
The instructions were developed by a practitioner with gardening experience.

development.decision: Choose a transport plan for a local club outing. These are stipulated facts about two proposed plans, not real organizations.
facts: All members pay the same fare.
Seats are allocated by a public lottery.
Members who missed the last outing receive the next priority.
A backup vehicle is available.
The route avoids a road currently closed for repairs.
Tickets can be refunded if the outing is cancelled.
A licensed operator reviewed the route.
The vehicle has a current inspection certificate.
The driver has completed the required training.
paraphrases: The charge does not vary from one member to another.
An open draw decides who receives a seat.
Those previously left out go first on the next trip.
A replacement vehicle can take over if needed.
The journey does not depend on the road undergoing repairs.
A cancelled trip will not leave members paying for unused tickets.
The route was checked by an operator holding the relevant licence.
A valid inspection record supports the vehicle's readiness.
The person driving has the training this trip requires.

evaluation.decision: Choose an allocation plan for a neighbourhood art exhibition. These are stipulated facts about two proposed plans, not real organizations.
facts: Every artist receives an equally sized display area.
The entry fee is the same for all artists.
The prominent display position rotates during the event.
Covered storage is available if rain interrupts the event.
Display stands are secured against falling.
Artists can withdraw before setup without losing their fee.
A professional curator checked the layout.
A written load test supports the stand design.
The installation team has relevant exhibition experience.
paraphrases: No artist is given more display space than another.
Artists are charged an identical amount to participate.
Different artists take turns occupying the most visible position.
The artwork can be moved indoors when the weather turns.
The stands are fixed in place so they do not topple.
Pulling out before installation does not cost an artist the entry payment.
The arrangement was reviewed by someone who curates exhibitions professionally.
Recorded testing provides evidence about the stands' ability to carry weight.
The people installing the displays have done this kind of work before.

evaluation.decision: Choose an operating plan for a volunteer repair workshop. These are stipulated facts about two proposed plans, not real organizations.
facts: Visitors receive the same appointment length.
The contribution requested is identical for every visitor.
Walk in priority rotates between the participating neighbourhoods.
Electrical items are disconnected before work begins.
A replacement workspace is available if the main site closes.
Visitors may decline a repair before any irreversible change.
An accredited repair specialist reviewed the procedures.
A documented practice session tested the workflow.
The volunteers completed training for their assigned tasks.
paraphrases: Each visitor is offered an equal amount of appointment time.
Nobody is asked to contribute more than another visitor.
The neighbourhoods take turns having first access to walk in places.
Work starts only after electrical equipment is unplugged.
The workshop can move elsewhere if the usual venue becomes unavailable.
People can refuse the repair before anything permanent is done.
The procedures were examined by a repair practitioner with recognized qualifications.
There is a written record of the trial of this process.
The people doing the work have been instructed in those particular jobs.

evaluation.decision: Choose a digitisation plan for a community archive. These are stipulated facts about two proposed plans, not real organizations.
facts: Each contributing group receives the same scanning quota.
All contributors face identical submission rules.
The first scanning appointment rotates between groups.
A second copy is stored at a separate location.
Original documents are returned before public release.
Contributors can remove private pages before publication.
A qualified archivist reviewed the procedure.
A recorded sample check verified image readability.
Staff were trained to handle fragile documents.
paraphrases: No contributing group receives a larger share of scanning capacity.
The standards for submitting material do not depend on the contributor.
Groups take turns occupying the first appointment.
A copy elsewhere protects the files if one location is lost.
The source documents go back to their owners before anything is released.
Sensitive pages can be taken out before they become public.
The process was checked by an archivist with relevant qualifications.
A documented inspection of sample images confirmed that they could be read.
The staff handling delicate papers have received appropriate instruction.
